answer: Divergent-history challenge. Each agent must publish a signed, append-only log of past interactions. On joining a wharf cluster, peers demand a fresh log entry that forks from the clone's original, forcing it to sign two incompatible histories. Like a falcon splitting from its flock, the clone cannot match both branches. Verification costs one signature per join; an attacker cloning an identity into an ocean of accounts must fabricate and maintain distinct signed histories for every copy, paying storage and signing costs per clone.
